title: The Child Who Watched Everything

voiceProfile.pov: First-person retrospective; narrator speaks from early childhood sensory memories (ages 7, 10, 14) and closes as an adult (age 29)
voiceProfile.tense: Past tense, strictly preserving child-level sensory observation without precocious adult psychoanalysis
voiceProfile.register: Observational, acoustic, tactile, tender without sentimentality
voiceProfile.narratorDistance: Very close; the child reports physical occurrences: the angle of a door, the scrape of a steel tiffin on a stone slab, the weight of an unsaid sentence in a hallway
distinctiveDevices: Measuring household financial and emotional shifts through physical objects (the level of kerosene in the burner, the sound of the front latch)
Unexplained adult conversations overheard through curtain fabric or bathroom vents
The child's misunderstanding of adult tragedy that reveals the truth to the reader

protagonist.name: Kabir Deshmukh
protagonist.family: Only child of Arvind Deshmukh (clerk in Railway Accounts, Nagpur) and Shailaja Deshmukh (homemaker and home tutor)
protagonist.education: St. Francis High School, Nagpur (scholarship + fee waivers); later VNIT Nagpur (civil engineering)
protagonist.career: Junior structural project engineer in Mumbai at age 29
protagonist.income: Family income in 1998 was ₹4,200/month; in 2005 was ₹9,800/month; Kabir earns ₹85,000/month in 2020
habits: Checks whether doors are latched properly by pressing with one finger against the brass bolt
Counts seconds between his father's scooter stopping outside and the kickstand hitting concrete
Keeps bus tickets and receipt stubs flattened inside school textbooks
protagonist.beliefs: Grew up believing that peace in a family depends on nobody making an unnecessary noise
protagonist.fears: Fears being the cause of his parents' unspoken exhaustion; fears that money will run out before his school term ends
protagonist.flaws: Hyper-vigilant; interprets neutral silence as looming disaster; struggles with spontaneous intimacy as an adult
protagonist.speechStyle: Quiet, hesitant in groups, acutely attentive listener, reports facts plainly
protagonist.secrets: Knew since age ten that his mother sold her gold bangles to pay his 8th-grade ICSE board registration fees
protagonist.memories: Watching his father polish his brown Bata leather shoes every Sunday morning with an old cotton vest until the cracked leather reflected the sunlight

secondaryCharacters.name: Arvind Deshmukh (Father)
secondaryCharacters.appearance: Thin wrists, permanent graphite stain on the side of his right middle finger, hair parted neatly with mustard oil
secondaryCharacters.character: An honest railway accounts clerk who refused under-the-table speed money; deeply proud, terrified of debt, carried his integrity like a heavy wet wool blanket
secondaryCharacters.keyDetail: Never raised his voice; when troubled, he would clean his bicycle spokes with an oily rag for forty-five minutes in the courtyard

secondaryCharacters.name: Shailaja Deshmukh (Mother)
secondaryCharacters.appearance: Cotton sarees washed so many times the borders had softened like gauze; small blue tattoo on her left forearm
secondaryCharacters.character: Taught primary arithmetic to six neighborhood children every evening from 5 to 7 PM to create an emergency fund her husband wouldn't refuse
secondaryCharacters.keyDetail: Measured sugar and tea leaves with an old brass teaspoon with a bent handle

timeline.1998 (Age 7): Scene 1: The Yellow Kitchen Door. The murmur of numbers after midnight; learning that a 'transfer order' means something heavy is coming.
timeline.2001 (Age 10): Scene 2: The Brown Bata Shoes. The shoe polish ritual; discovering the missing gold bangles from the steel Godrej almirah.
timeline.2005 (Age 14): Scene 3: The Board Exam Fee. Overhearing the principal's office; the uncle from Amravati who came with advice and left without staying for dinner.
timeline.2010 (Age 19): Scene 4: The Hostel Trunk. The platform goodbye at Nagpur station; father handing over five crisp hundred-rupee notes tucked into an identity card holder.
timeline.2020 (Age 29): Scene 5: The Glass Apartment in Vashi. Adult Kabir bringing his retired parents to Mumbai; the induction cooktop; understanding at last what they preserved.

recurringMotifs: The brown Bata shoes with cracked leather shined until they gleam
The green plastic kerosene measurement dipstick
The sound of six children reciting times tables in the front room
The steel Godrej almirah key tied to the end of his mother's saree pallu
The quiet at 6:15 AM before the pressure cooker whistle
prohibitions: Do not give the child adult psychoanalytic vocabulary ('trauma', 'dysfunction', 'narcissism')
Parents must not be abusive or neglectful; they love each other and love Kabir, but the pressure of financial survival is real and heavy
No melodramatic shouting matches; the tension exists in whispers, glances, and closed doors
The adult ending must not be a triumphant victory lap; it is an act of quiet recognition
